questions.label: Q3(a)
questions.sharedContext:
Conditional Probability

Before going on vacation for a week, you ask your spacey friend to water your ailing plant. Without water, the plant has a 70 percent chance of dying. Even with proper watering, it has a 10 percent chance of dying. And the probability that your friend will forget to water it is 25 percent.

Either create the expected frequency tree or use Bayes’ theorem alongside the appropriate probability rules and use that to calculate the probabilities for the following questions:
questions.text: (a) What’s the chance that your plant will survive the week? [3 points]
questions.modelAnswer:
$$P(\text{survive}) = P(\text{survive} \mid \text{watered})P(\text{watered}) + P(\text{survive} \mid \text{forgot})P(\text{forgot})$$

$$= 0.90 \times 0.75 + 0.30 \times 0.25 = 0.675 + 0.075 = 0.75$$

The chance that your plant will survive the week is 75%.

questions.label: Q3(b)
questions.sharedContext:
Conditional Probability

Before going on vacation for a week, you ask your spacey friend to water your ailing plant. Without water, the plant has a 70 percent chance of dying. Even with proper watering, it has a 10 percent chance of dying. And the probability that your friend will forget to water it is 25 percent.

Either create the expected frequency tree or use Bayes’ theorem alongside the appropriate probability rules and use that to calculate the probabilities for the following questions:
questions.text: (b) If it’s dead when you return, what’s the chance that your friend forgot to water it? [3 points]
questions.modelAnswer:
$$P(\text{dead}) = 0.10 \times 0.75 + 0.70 \times 0.25 = 0.075 + 0.175 = 0.25$$

$$P(\text{forgot} \mid \text{dead}) = \frac{P(\text{dead} \mid \text{forgot})P(\text{forgot})}{P(\text{dead})} = \frac{0.70 \times 0.25}{0.25} = 0.70$$

If it’s dead when you return, the chance that your friend forgot to water it is 70%.

questions.label: Q3(c)
questions.sharedContext:
Conditional Probability

Before going on vacation for a week, you ask your spacey friend to water your ailing plant. Without water, the plant has a 70 percent chance of dying. Even with proper watering, it has a 10 percent chance of dying. And the probability that your friend will forget to water it is 25 percent.

Either create the expected frequency tree or use Bayes’ theorem alongside the appropriate probability rules and use that to calculate the probabilities for the following questions:

questions.modelAnswer:
$$P(\text{alive} \mid \text{forgot}) = 1 - P(\text{dead} \mid \text{forgot}) = 1 - 0.70 = 0.30$$

If your friend forgot to water it, the chance it’ll be alive when you return is 30%.

questions.label: Q4
questions.text:
Design a Research Study

A regional government has issued a large study of the high schools in the region. As part of this study, an overview has been made of both the central exam and the school exam results of all students in the region. Note that in the Netherlands, someone’s graduation grades are determined based on both these results. For each student, it is listed what grades were obtained for which course. Moreover, it is also known which teachers taught each course to the students and at which school they taught the course. Based on the average grades per school (for the central exam) that were calculated based on this information and subsequently communicated to the schools, the top school (highest average grades on the central exam) requests another analysis to be performed on the data.

The school requests the following analysis to be performed :

1. How do our students perform on each subject relative to the other schools in the region? Specifically, are there courses where our students under-perform relative to the other schools in the region?
2. Are the findings about performance across courses consistent across teachers?

Describe your approach to process the data described above (note that it has already been collected) in such a way as to answer the research questions above. Consider the full process of setting up the analysis. Do not worry about how this would done in Python/elsewhere (that is, don’t write pseudocode, focus on how the analysis would be performed and what you would assess).
questions.modelAnswer:
A full-credit answer should describe the complete analysis process:

- Define the observational units: student-course exam results, with school, teacher, course, central exam grade, and school exam grade.
- Clean and validate the data, checking missing values, duplicates, inconsistent course labels, teacher identifiers, and impossible grade values.
- Restrict or flag analyses to comparable courses and exam types, especially central exam grades because the research question refers to central exam performance.
- For each subject, compare the top school’s students to students from other schools in the region using subject-specific summaries such as means, standard deviations, sample sizes, confidence intervals, and differences in means.
- Assess uncertainty rather than only ranking schools, because some courses may have few students.
- Identify courses where the top school under-performs relative to the regional comparison, using estimated differences and confidence intervals or suitable hypothesis tests.
- Account for relevant structure in the data: students are nested within courses, teachers, and schools, and course difficulty and student composition may differ.
- For consistency across teachers, repeat the subject-level comparisons within teacher groups where possible, or use a model with teacher effects and school/course effects.
- Check whether under-performance is concentrated among particular teachers or appears across teachers teaching the same course.
- Report limitations: the data are observational, so the analysis can compare performance but cannot by itself prove that a school or teacher caused the differences.

questions.label: Q5(a)
questions.sharedContext:
Video game genres

A survey of 1200 teens collected data about video game use by teens. According to the survey, the following are among the most popular game genres:

| Genre | Examples | Percent who play |
|---|---|---:|
| Racing | NASCAR, Mario Kart, Burnout | 70 |
| Sports | Madden, FIFA, Tony Hawk | 65 |
| Rhythm | Guitar Hero, Dance Dance Revolution, Lumines | 61 |
questions.text: Give a 95% confidence interval for the proportion who play games in each of these three genres. Make sure to note the correct formula and how/why you are applying it to calculate the confidence limits.
questions.modelAnswer:
Use the large-sample confidence interval for a proportion:

$$\hat{p} \pm 1.96\sqrt{\frac{\hat{p}(1 - \hat{p})}{n}}$$

This applies because the sample size is $n = 1200$ and the expected numbers of successes and failures are large for all three genres.

Racing: $\hat{p} = 0.70$

$$0.70 \pm 1.96\sqrt{\frac{0.70(0.30)}{1200}} = 0.70 \pm 0.0259$$

95% CI: $(0.674, 0.726)$, or 67.4% to 72.6%.

Sports: $\hat{p} = 0.65$

$$0.65 \pm 1.96\sqrt{\frac{0.65(0.35)}{1200}} = 0.65 \pm 0.0270$$

95% CI: $(0.623, 0.677)$, or 62.3% to 67.7%.

Rhythm: $\hat{p} = 0.61$

$$0.61 \pm 1.96\sqrt{\frac{0.61(0.39)}{1200}} = 0.61 \pm 0.0276$$

95% CI: $(0.582, 0.638)$, or 58.2% to 63.8%.

questions.label: Q5(b)
questions.sharedContext:
Video game genres

A survey of 1200 teens collected data about video game use by teens. According to the survey, the following are among the most popular game genres:

| Genre | Examples | Percent who play |
|---|---|---:|
| Racing | NASCAR, Mario Kart, Burnout | 70 |
| Sports | Madden, FIFA, Tony Hawk | 65 |
| Rhythm | Guitar Hero, Dance Dance Revolution, Lumines | 61 |
questions.text: Explain why the chance that at least one of your intervals does not contain the true value of the parameter (that is, the population percentage of teens playing any of these genres of games) is greater than the $α$ of 5% that we set for the confidence interval in part (a).
questions.modelAnswer:
Each 95% confidence interval has a 5% error rate when considered on its own. In part (a), three intervals are constructed. The probability that all three intervals contain their true parameters is less than 95%, so the probability that at least one interval misses its true parameter is greater than 5%.

If the intervals were independent, the probability that at least one misses would be:

$$1 - 0.95^3 = 0.142625$$

or about 14.3%. Even without assuming independence, doing multiple confidence intervals increases the chance of at least one error compared with a single interval.

questions.label: Q6(a)
questions.sharedContext:
Box of cereal

A packaging company is asked by a producer of cereal to fill boxes of their newest brand. The cereal company would like to have at least 200 grams of cereal in their boxes and they are willing to accept that in general, five out of a thousand boxes are filled with less than 200 grams. Suppose the packaging company has a filling machine that fills boxes with a weight that is normally distributed with an unknown mean and a known standard deviation of 4 grams. Upon an inspection of 16 boxes that were filled by the machine, the company found that the boxes were filled with sample mean 211 grams.
questions.text: Construct a 95% confidence interval of the mean for the weight of the cereal box.
questions.modelAnswer:
Because the population standard deviation is known, use a $z$ confidence interval:

$$\bar{x} \pm 1.96\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}}$$

With $\bar{x}=211$, $\sigma=4$, and $n=16$:

$$211 \pm 1.96\frac{4}{\sqrt{16}} = 211 \pm 1.96$$

95% confidence interval:

$$(209.04, 212.96)$$

So the 95% confidence interval for the mean weight is 209.04 grams to 212.96 grams.

questions.label: Q6(b)
questions.sharedContext:
Box of cereal

A packaging company is asked by a producer of cereal to fill boxes of their newest brand. The cereal company would like to have at least 200 grams of cereal in their boxes and they are willing to accept that in general, five out of a thousand boxes are filled with less than 200 grams. Suppose the packaging company has a filling machine that fills boxes with a weight that is normally distributed with an unknown mean and a known standard deviation of 4 grams. Upon an inspection of 16 boxes that were filled by the machine, the company found that the boxes were filled with sample mean 211 grams.
questions.text:
After further analysis of the initial output of the machine, the company finds that the machine fills boxes with a mean of 211 grams.

Based on this information, does the machine adhere to the standards that the cereal company demanded (i.e., at most five out of a thousand boxes are filled with less than 400 grams)?
questions.modelAnswer:
The standard in the setup is at most five out of a thousand boxes below 200 grams. Using the stated normal distribution with mean $\mu = 211$ and standard deviation $\sigma = 4$:

$$P(X < 200) = P\left(Z < \frac{200 - 211}{4}\right) = P(Z < -2.75)$$

$$P(Z < -2.75) \approx 0.0030$$

This is about 3 boxes per 1000, which is less than 5 boxes per 1000. Therefore, using the 200 gram standard described in the setup, the machine adheres to the cereal company’s demand.

If the threshold is read literally as 400 grams in the final sentence, then no: since the machine has mean 211 grams, essentially all boxes would be below 400 grams. This appears inconsistent with the earlier 200 gram standard.

questions.sharedContext:
Correlation

Suppose the correlation coefficient between an independent and a dependent variable is $− 0 . 80$ and the spearman rank correlation is $− 0 . 75$ .

Statement : Below-mean values of the dependent variable (relative to its own mean) are associated with below-mean values of the independent variable (relative to its own mean).
questions.text: Is the statement true or false?
questions.modelAnswer: False

questions.label: Q8(b)
questions.sharedContext:
Correlation

Suppose the correlation coefficient between an independent and a dependent variable is $− 0 . 80$ and the spearman rank correlation is $− 0 . 75$ .

Statement : Below-mean values of the dependent variable (relative to its own mean) are associated with below-mean values of the independent variable (relative to its own mean).
questions.text: Your motivation on why the statement is either true or false and why the spearman rank correlation matters to explain this:
questions.modelAnswer:
The statement is false. A correlation coefficient of $-0.80$ means that values above the mean on one variable tend to be associated with values below the mean on the other variable, and values below the mean on one variable tend to be associated with values above the mean on the other variable. The statement describes a positive association, not a negative one.

The Spearman rank correlation of $-0.75$ matters because it shows that the negative association is also present in the ranked data. This means the relationship is not only a linear negative relationship measured by Pearson correlation, but also a strong negative monotonic relationship in the ranks.

    for each column in df:
